sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3! Closed-form triplet inversion encounters two production hazards: near-zero denominator pairs Sigma k l close to zero, and global sign flip symmetry between positive z and negative z. Select the numerical safeguard suite that prevents both failures.

sentences.text: Final checkpoint! Remember that minus z times minus z transpose equals plus z times plus z transpose, and dividing by tiny Sigma k l blows up estimates. Which safeguard suite resolves both hazards?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding numerical engineering! Option B is correct. Threshold-gating auxiliary pairs above min triplet cov, aggregating via robust median, and enforcing positive average domain correlation sum of z j greater than zero prevents both variance blowups and inverted class flips!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Option B is correct. Averaging unclipped ratios or ignoring sign symmetry amplifies divide-by-zero spikes and risks flipping predictions globally. You must gate denominator magnitude, aggregate with median, and enforce sum of z j greater than zero.
